subtopic: Handling a leaked photo or online harassment
subtype: Approach: staying calm and not replying in anger [Thinking]
passage: The photo appeared in the class group at twenty to ten: a private one of Pranav, meant for a single friend. His face went hot, then cold. His thumbs were already typing, Who did this??? and worse. He looked at the words, then deleted them. If he fired back, they would screenshot that too, and it would become a fight instead of a wrong done to him. He put the phone face down and breathed until his hands stopped shaking. Then he called his cousin Kunal, who told him, “Don't answer anyone. Go to your mother now.” Pranav walked into the living room. His mother listened, put an arm round him, said, “This is not your fault,” and picked up the phone to call the school's safety lead that night.

qa.q: What did Pranav do with the angry message he typed?
qa.a: He deleted it.

qa.q: What was Pranav feeling when the photo appeared?
qa.a: Panic and rage: his face went hot, then cold, and his thumbs began typing angry words.

qa.q: What could Pranav do next, and why?
qa.a: Save screenshots with dates and share them with the school, since adults can act on real proof.

qa.q: How does the night look to Pranav's mother?
qa.a: Pranav's mother is shocked and worried but glad he came to her, and phoning the school safety lead the same night gives her something useful to do.

grounding: A teen who sees a private photo shared in a class group decides an angry reply would fuel it and goes to an adult first.

subtopic: Handling a leaked photo or online harassment
subtype: Approach: saving evidence before anything is deleted [Action]
passage: Tuesday, late. I took screenshots of everything before it could vanish: the messages, the names of who sent them, the dates and times. I saved the links, too. Then I put it all in one private folder and wrote a list on paper, in order: what, who, when. I did not reply to anyone, though I wanted to. Amma saw me at the desk and read over my shoulder, and she sat down and put her hand over mine. She said, “This is not your fault.” She said we'd take the folder to Urmila ma'am at school first thing, and she rang to ask if we could come at eight. I still feel shaky, but I'm not carrying it by myself tonight. — Santosh

qa.q: Where did Santosh keep the screenshots?
qa.a: In one private folder.

qa.q: How does Santosh feel at the end of the entry?
qa.a: Shaky but a little steadier: the evidence is saved and Amma is on Santosh's side.

qa.q: What else could Santosh do to protect the proof, and why?
qa.a: Keep a second copy somewhere safe and delete nothing, since deleted messages cannot be checked later.

qa.q: How does the folder look to Urmila ma'am?
qa.a: Urmila ma'am gets real dates and names instead of only a story, so the school can act through its own process.

grounding: A student saves screenshots showing messages, names and dates, so that adults, the school or police can act on real proof.

subtopic: Handling a leaked photo or online harassment
subtype: Approach: telling a trusted adult right away [Action]
passage:
Monday night. Ganga sat on her bed with the phone face down. It buzzed again and again. She felt ashamed and alone, and every time she thought of telling somebody, her throat closed. She didn't sleep.
Tuesday morning. At breakfast she said, “Mummy, something happened,” and the words came out in pieces. Mummy put her spoon down, held her, and said, “Thank you for telling me. This is not your fault.” They rang the school before eight.
Thursday. Sarita ma'am, the class teacher, met them with the safety lead. Together they wrote a plan: who would be told, what would be saved, and who would check on Ganga each day. Ganga's shoulders came down from around her ears for the first time in days.

qa.q: Who did Ganga tell first?
qa.a: Mummy, at breakfast.

qa.q: How did Ganga feel on Monday night?
qa.a: Ashamed and alone: her throat closed each time she thought of telling somebody.

qa.q: What was the turning point, and why did it help?
qa.a: Telling Mummy at breakfast, because it turned a secret carried alone into a plan shared with adults.

qa.q: How does the situation look to Sarita ma'am?
qa.a: Sarita ma'am meets a frightened student and her mother after a call, and wants to protect Ganga and follow the school's process without blaming her.

grounding: A teen tells her mother and class teacher what happened, despite shame, and they plan next steps together.

subtopic: Handling a leaked photo or online harassment
subtype: Approach: using platform reporting and official complaint routes [Action]
passage: Nadia's father Gabriel set the laptop on the kitchen table in Montreal, with Nadia sitting beside him. First they used the report button on the app to ask for the images to be taken down, and screenshotted the confirmation. Then Gabriel filled in the online form on the official police cybercrime site while Nadia's mother read out the dates and names from the list. On Monday they met the school's safety lead, who said the school has a written policy, that staff would deal with the group chat, and that sharing pictures of a young person is treated as a serious matter. Nobody, the lead said, should forward the pictures, even to warn others. Nadia said very little, but she didn't leave the room.

qa.q: Where did Gabriel file the complaint?
qa.a: On the official police cybercrime site.

qa.q: What might Nadia have been feeling at the kitchen table?
qa.a: Anxious and exposed, but supported: she said very little, yet stayed in the room with her parents.

qa.q: What else could the family do, and why?
qa.a: Ask the school counsellor to check in with Nadia, since practical reports help but Nadia also needs emotional support.

qa.q: How does the evening look to Gabriel?
qa.a: Gabriel is probably angry and protective, and filling in forms gives him a concrete way to help his daughter.

grounding: A family reports images to the app, files an official complaint and the school follows its safety policy.

subtopic: Handling a leaked photo or online harassment
subtype: Approach: blaming the victim and hiding [Pitfall]
passage:
Bhavna: Where were you today? Ma'am asked about you.
Nikita: Not coming this week. I deleted everything.
Bhavna: Everything? Nikita, why?
Nikita: It's my fault. I should never have sent it.
Bhavna: It isn't your fault. Whoever shared it did the wrong thing.
Nikita: Everyone has seen it. I can't face anyone.
Bhavna: Please let me come over. Or tell your parents?
Nikita: No. Don't tell anyone. I'm switching off my phone.
Bhavna: I can't leave it. I'm telling my mum I'm worried and I'm coming at five.
(Nikita's phone showed offline. At five Bhavna's mum was already on the phone to Nikita's parents.)

qa.q: What did Nikita delete?
qa.a: Nikita deleted everything.

qa.q: What is Nikita feeling in this chat?
qa.a: Shame and self-blame: Nikita says it is Nikita's own fault and cannot face anyone.

qa.q: What could Nikita do instead of hiding, and why?
qa.a: Talk to a trusted adult, since the fault lies with whoever shared the picture and help can stop it spreading.

qa.q: How does the situation look to Bhavna?
qa.a: Bhavna is worried and feels helpless because Nikita is cutting off contact, so Bhavna asks a mother for help.

grounding: A teen decides it is all the teen's fault, deletes accounts and avoids school, cutting off the people who could help.

subtopic: Handling a leaked photo or online harassment
subtype: Approach: retaliating by leaking something back [Pitfall]
passage:
Monday. A private photo of Sumit was passed around the year group. He was sure it was a classmate who'd been rude to him all term.
Tuesday. Rage sat in his chest like a stone. That evening he found an embarrassing picture of that classmate and posted it in a big group chat, with a mocking line. It got forty reactions in an hour. For a few minutes it felt like winning.
Thursday. Minakshi ma'am, the year head, called Sumit in. The classmate's parents had complained. “Your photo being shared was wrong, and we are dealing with it,” she said. “But what you posted is wrong too, and it may count against you.” Sumit stared at his shoes. He had turned from the one wronged into the one explaining himself.

qa.q: Who did Sumit think had shared his photo?
qa.a: A classmate who had been rude to him all term.

qa.q: What was Sumit feeling on Tuesday evening when he posted the picture?
qa.a: Rage and hurt, and a need to hit back, which briefly felt like winning.

qa.q: What could Sumit have done instead of posting, and why?
qa.a: Save proof and tell a teacher or parent, since that keeps him as the person who was wronged and lets adults act.

qa.q: How does the situation look to the classmate?
qa.a: The classmate now has something to point at and can claim to be the one wronged, and is also embarrassed and upset by the posted picture.

grounding: A student retaliates by posting an embarrassing picture of the classmate he suspects, turning himself from victim into wrongdoer.

subtopic: Handling a leaked photo or online harassment
subtype: Approach: blocking, muting and tightening privacy settings [Action]
passage: I blocked all four accounts that had been sending things. Then I opened my settings and limited who could message me or tag me, so only people I know can get through. I changed my passwords and made each one different. Last, I messaged my close friends, including Imran, and asked them plainly not to forward anything, not even to say look at this. Imran wrote back within a minute: “I won't. I'm sorry this is happening.” The complaint was already with the school, so none of this fixed everything. But my phone was quieter, and I felt a bit lighter, as if I'd closed a few windows against the wind. — Pooja

qa.q: Who did Pooja ask not to forward anything?
qa.a: Close friends, including Imran.

qa.q: How did Pooja feel after doing these steps?
qa.a: A little lighter and safer, though the situation was not fixed.

qa.q: What else could Pooja add, and why?
qa.a: Ask a trusted adult to check the privacy settings together and keep the evidence, since a second pair of eyes may catch what was missed.

qa.q: How does the request look to Imran?
qa.a: Imran feels trusted and wants to help, and being asked plainly reminds Imran that even forwarding to warn others adds to the harm.

grounding: A teen blocks harassing accounts, limits messages and tags, changes passwords and asks friends not to forward anything.

subtopic: Handling a leaked photo or online harassment
subtype: Approach: getting emotional support alongside practical steps [Revision]
passage:
Tuesday. Nitin had done everything on the checklist: the screenshots were saved, the complaint was in, the accounts were blocked. It felt like enough.
Saturday. Nitin was still sleeping badly and had a knot in the stomach on the way to school. Something was not fading. That evening Nitin thought, the checklist covers what to do, not how I am.
Monday. Nitin went to the school counsellor. The counsellor said, “I'm glad you came. What you feel makes sense.” They agreed to meet each week, and the counsellor offered to be with Nitin when telling the parents that afternoon.
Thursday. Nitin's cousin Gargi came over and they walked to the park, as they now do every Thursday, and just talked.

qa.q: Who did Nitin add to the plan besides the counsellor?
qa.a: Cousin Gargi, for regular talks.

qa.q: What did Nitin feel when noticing that the stress was not fading after the practical steps?
qa.a: Worry and unease: Nitin was still sleeping badly and felt a knot in the stomach on the way to school.

qa.q: What could Nitin do if things still feel heavy after some weeks, and why?
qa.a: Tell the counsellor and parents again, since more support may be needed and it is fine to ask.

qa.q: How does Nitin's reaching out look to Gargi?
qa.a: Gargi feels trusted by being chosen to talk with, and the weekly walks give Gargi a clear way to help.

grounding: A teen still sleeping badly notices the stress is not fading, tells the school counsellor and adds talks with a trusted cousin.

subtopic: Handling a leaked photo or online harassment
subtype: Approach: root-cause thinking about how the image got out [Thinking]
passage: In the counsellor Binita's room, Raghav drew arrows on a whiteboard. Tuesday: the picture was sent to one friend. Thursday: it appeared in the group. He pulled out a screenshot, showing which account posted it first, then went quiet. “The first post came from the friend's own phone,” he said slowly. Binita ma'am only asked, “What does that tell you?” Raghav thought aloud. “Not that my friend did it. The phone has no lock, and it stays in the bag at gym time. Someone else could have copied it.” He wrote three lines: tell the friend gently, tell the school with the timeline, and from now on keep private things off any phone that is not locked. Raghav put down the marker. It didn't erase the hurt, but it gave the mess a shape.

qa.q: Where did the first post come from, in the end?
qa.a: From the friend's own phone.

qa.q: What did Raghav feel when he saw the source of the first post?
qa.a: Shocked and torn: he went quiet, hurt but still wanting to be fair to the friend.

qa.q: What else could Raghav do with this finding, and why?
qa.a: Tell the friend gently so they can lock their phone, since the friend may not know how the picture got out.

qa.q: How might the friend feel when told?
qa.a: The friend may feel guilty and scared, and needs to hear that nobody thinks they did it on purpose.

grounding: A student traces how a picture spread, finds a trusted friend's phone was the source and plans who should be told and how private data is kept safe.

subtopic: Handling a leaked photo or online harassment
subtype: Approach: helping a friend who is being targeted [Action]
passage: Rafiq noticed it during computer period: a classmate, Tanya, being mocked in the group chat, with joke after joke about a photo of her. Nobody stopped. Rafiq didn't add a laugh and didn't forward anything. Instead, Rafiq took screenshots of the messages, the names and the times. At the break Rafiq sent Tanya a private message: “I saw. I'm sorry. It's not okay. Do you want company?” Tanya replied after a minute: “Yes.” They met at the library. “Shall we tell Dhruv Sir together?” Rafiq asked. Tanya nodded, though her hands shook. Dhruv Sir listened, thanked them both for bringing the screenshots, and said he'd pass it to the safety lead that day and keep her name out of it.

qa.q: What did Rafiq do with the messages?
qa.a: Took screenshots of the messages, names and times.

qa.q: How might Tanya have felt when Rafiq's private message arrived?
qa.a: Relieved that someone cared, though still embarrassed and shaky about what had happened.

qa.q: What else could Rafiq do to support Tanya, and why?
qa.a: Keep checking in and sit with Tanya at lunch, since a friend nearby can make going to school easier.

qa.q: How does the situation look to Dhruv Sir?
qa.a: Dhruv Sir sees two students bringing proof and asking for help, so he can act the same day without exposing Tanya.

grounding: A teen who sees a classmate mocked in a group chat does not join in, checks on her privately, saves the messages and goes to a teacher together.
